ops.title: Worker-spawned launchctl bootstrap fails EIO where interactive launchctl succeeds (caller-context dependence)
ops.premise: launchctl bootstrap invoked through daemonkit's worker machinery fails with EIO 5 for GUI .app-Program and session-keyed jobs while the identical bootstrap succeeds from an interactive shell — the caller's execution context (spawn attributes, audit session, responsibility, environment, or the worker indirection itself) is causal, not plist content.

ops.text: Five plist-content mechanisms falsified with controlled tests (2026-07-26, fleet task fc39f885 + backlog 574ba471): key presence (sleep+Aqua manual bootstrap exit 0; host.v1 loaded carrying Aqua), .app-Program discriminator (home's failing helper was a plain Caskroom binary), per-label launchd DB wedge (home's label was virgin), session-type mismatch (local desired==current==Aqua), and bootout-to-bootstrap teardown window (EIO against a 90-second-absent label).

Decisive falsifier (local machine, captain-hook 12.20.11 on daemonkit v0.20.8): the exact same keyless plist EIOs through daemonkit's install path (6 attempts) and bootstraps exit-0 instantly by hand, twice. Process lineage of the failure: brew -> Cellar capt-hookd package-install -> (launchctl) grandchild + (capt-hookd) worker child. Every recorded success across both machines ran launchctl as a child of an interactive Aqua shell.

Cross-machine matrix by caller x program x key: daemonkit-caller x plain-exe x keyless SUCCEEDS (home serve/reconcile via Converge over SSH); daemonkit-caller x plain-exe x Background-key FAILS (home reposync helper, fresh label); daemonkit-caller x .app x Aqua-key and x keyless both FAIL (local, pre- and post-fix); manual x anything SUCCEEDS (4 recorded). The caller-context factor interacts with job complexity - launchd appears stricter with non-interactive callers for GUI-app or session-keyed jobs.

launchctl managername returns Aqua from inside the failing brew-grandchild context, so the effect is not a naive session-manager mismatch; audit-session shape, Mach bootstrap port inheritance through the worker spawn, posix_spawn attributes (setsid/session flags), and brew's scrubbed environment remain the live candidates.

Field cost of each failed attempt (measured): host daemon cycled, helper booted out and not restored, no bundle delivery (delivery gates behind agent install, captain-hook dc97d32). Reinstall guard re-imposed hard on the local machine; manual bootstrap is the recovery. applyRolledBack recovery (v0.20.8) field-confirmed working twice during these attempts - receipts are not the problem.
